seo_meta_description: Master Mean Median Mode for Digital SAT Math with concise concept summaries, 20+ graded practice questions with Desmos shortcuts, formula cheat sheet, and 3-level mock test.

concepts.summary: The mean is the sum of all values divided by the total count of values.
key_rules: Effect of adding a constant $k$ to every term: $\text{New Mean} = \text{Old Mean} + k$
Effect of multiplying every term by $k$: $\text{New Mean} = \text{Old Mean} \times k$
concepts.traditional_method: Sum the data points and divide by the number of entries $n$.
concepts.sat_speed_trick: Use the Desmos 'mean()' function by typing the list into a variable, e.g., L = [x1, x2, x3], then typing mean(L).

worked_example.problem: The mean of 5 numbers is 12. If a 6th number, 18, is added, what is the new mean?
traditional_solution: Step 2: Add the new number to the sum: $60 + 18 = 78$
Step 3: Divide by the new count: $78 / 6 = 13$
speed_trick: Step 2: Type mean(L) in a new line

concepts.summary: The median is the middle value of a data set when ordered from least to greatest.
key_rules: For even $n$: $\text{Median} = \text{average of values at } n/2 \text{ and } (n/2)+1$
The median is resistant to outliers, unlike the mean.
concepts.traditional_method: Sort the data set in ascending order and identify the middle term.
concepts.sat_speed_trick: Use the Desmos 'median()' function on a defined list.

worked_example.problem: Find the median of the set: {15, 3, 8, 12, 20, 5}.
traditional_solution: Step 2: Identify the two middle terms: 8 and 12
speed_trick: Step 2: Type median(L) in a new line

concepts.summary: The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set.
key_rules: A set can have one mode, multiple modes (multimodal), or no mode.
If all values appear with the same frequency, there is no mode.
The mode is the peak of a frequency histogram.
concepts.traditional_method: Create a frequency table to count occurrences of each value.
concepts.sat_speed_trick: Use the 'dotplot' or 'histogram' visualization in Desmos if data is provided in a table.

concepts.summary: The mean is sensitive to extreme values (outliers), while the median is robust.
key_rules: If the distribution is skewed right, $\text{Mean} > \text{Median}$
If the distribution is skewed left, $\text{Mean} < \text{Median}$
concepts.traditional_method: Compare the impact of adding a large value to the mean versus the median.
concepts.sat_speed_trick: Test with a small set: {1, 2, 3} vs {1, 2, 100}.

sat_traps.title: The 'Average of Averages' Trap
sat_traps.description: Never average two means unless the sample sizes are identical. Always calculate the total sum first.

sat_traps.title: The 'Missing Value' Trap
sat_traps.description: Forgetting to account for the new total count $n$ when adding a value to a set.

practice_questions.question: The mode of a set of 7 integers is 10. If the set is $\{8, 10, 12, x, 10, 15, 9\}$, what must be true about $x$?
practice_questions.hint: The mode is the most frequent number. If 10 is the mode, it must appear more than any other number.
traditional_solution: Step 1: Count current frequencies: 10 appears twice, others appear once.
Step 2: To keep 10 as the mode, $x$ cannot create a new mode.
Step 3: If $x = 10$, the mode is still 10. If $x \neq 10$, the mode is still 10.
Step 4: Actually, $x$ can be anything, but the question implies $x$ is not 10 to maintain the current set structure.
speed_trick: Step 2: If $x=10$, 10 appears 3 times. If $x=5$, 10 appears 2 times. Both keep 10 as the mode.
Step 3: The most restrictive condition is $x \neq 10$ is not required, but $x$ cannot be a number that appears twice.
